To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) high‐resolution cationic contrast enhanced μCT is a useful technique to assess articular cartilage composition, morphology, and degeneration in mouse models of osteoarthritis; 2) cationic contrast agents may be more sensitive than anionic agents for detecting changes in proteoglycan content; and 3) the high‐resolution μCT technique is precise, with measurement errors of 2.5%–8%.
